text: According to the chapter, the deep reason elementary geometry (RCF) is decidable while arithmetic is not is that:
choices: geometry has fewer axioms than arithmetic
geometry is second-order while arithmetic is first-order
the integers ℤ are not first-order definable in a real-closed field, so it cannot interpret arithmetic
geometric proofs never appeal to infinity
explanation: By quantifier elimination, every definable subset of the line in a real-closed field is semialgebraic (a finite union of points and intervals), but ℤ is infinite and discrete, so no formula defines it. Without ℤ one cannot interpret arithmetic, build Gödel codes, or diagonalize — 'geometry is decidable precisely because it cannot count.' It is not a matter of axiom count, logical order, or infinity.
